clue.text: Once again holds mount back, handier than the rest

indicators.note: one word holds another, keeping it inside its own letters

parts.note: eft is an archaic word for again or afterwards

indicators.note: going back means the word for mount is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to mount a jewel is to set it

explanation.surface: Someone recalls an old rider who kept their horse in check and was the handiest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: EFT, the archaic adverb, holds TES. EFT is also a Scots adjective meaning handy, so EFTEST is its superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Eft in Scots means convenient or handy, and the superlative form means the most convenient of all.

clue.text: Naughty imp is pert, unruly — describe when had up (12, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up turns it so it reads bottom to top
unruly letters will not stay in line, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: these six letters are rearranged
to describe something is to tell of it

explanation.surface: A cheeky, disobedient imp is described as it is hauled before the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had up' sounds like being charged in court; here it only turns 'tell of' upside down in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An esprit follet is French for a mischievous goblin or sprite, a playful household spirit.

clue.text: Jewish community from Florida having a whip round? Au contraire

indicators.text: having a whip round? Au contraire
indicators.note: having something round you means enclosing it, and 'au contraire' flips which word is outside, so the place wraps the lash

parts.note: Chambers lists FA as an abbreviation for Florida
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: Members of a Jewish community in Florida hold a whip-round, a collection of money among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a British term for an informal collection. Taken straight, A LASH would hold Florida; 'au contraire' reverses that, so F...A holds A LASH. FA for Florida is rare outside Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Falasha are the Ethiopian Jewish people, now usually called Beta Israel.

clue.text: Bundle consisting of Irish coats but no tie

indicators.note: 'but no' tells you to take the following letters away from the word before

parts.note: a trusty is an Irish word for a heavy greatcoat
these three letters are removed, wherever they sit

explanation.surface: A parcel of Irish overcoats, packed without any neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters T, I and E are not together in TRUSTIES; each is struck out separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a bundle, as of hay or straw, tied up for carrying.

clue.text: Sentence to carve below stone head of repository

indicators.note: in a down light, one part placed below another simply comes after it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for the stone weight

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of repository
to etch is to carve lines into a surface

explanation.surface: An instruction to carve something beneath a stone in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is slang for a prison sentence, a term served inside.

clue.text: Light vehicle beside shambling nag

indicators.note: a shambling gait is disordered and awkward, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: to can mean close by or against, as in 'face to face'
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small cart pulled along next to a worn-out, shuffling horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled carriage used in India.

clue.text: Fermented dairy product? what shall I say?? gobbled by plonker?

indicators.note: something gobbled by another ends up inside it

parts.note: Chambers gives a plonker as a loud, smacking kiss
um is the hesitant sound of someone searching for words

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over what to call a dairy drink while a fool wolfs it down.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is everyday British slang for an idiot; the clue uses a rarer Chambers sense, a smacking kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Kumiss is the fermented mare's milk drunk across the Central Asian steppe.

clue.text: Where tribal elders meet king dropping in, voice raised

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so those letters are lost

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

indicators.note: raised in a down light means turned to read upward

parts.note: an alto is a singing voice

explanation.surface: The meeting place of tribal elders, where a king drops in and voices are raised in debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping in' reads as a visit; instead, the letters I and N drop out of KING.
explanation.definitionFit: A kgotla is the traditional village assembly or meeting place in Botswana.

clue.text: Number two's second after word number one brought up

definitions.note: uncountable noun, matching the mass sense of the answer

indicators.note: one piece placed after the others simply comes at the end

parts.note: mot is French for word, as in bon mot

indicators.note: brought up in a down light means turned to read from the bottom

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number, and I is one
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Toilet humour: the deputy comes second after the leader has spoken and been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Number two is nursery slang for excrement.
explanation.definitionFit: Motions, like number two, is a polite term for faeces or a bowel movement.

clue.text: How many prefer Scotch, fierce in tangle with English

indicators.note: a tangle has its strands knotted out of order, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, ready for rearranging
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Many fierce Scots take their whisky tangled up with an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch here is whisky; purists drink it with no ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty of whisky drinkers take their Scotch without ice, so they like it free of ice.

clue.text: Bondman, somewhat brisk when cut up

indicators.note: up in a down light means the letters climb, reading bottom to top
somewhat means only part of the word, so its end is lost

parts.note: a brisk wind is a fresh one

explanation.surface: A labourer who is rather brisk and gets cross when cut up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bondman is a man bound in servitude to a lord, as a serf was.

clue.text: Being gormless, Scots hens running about in puddle copy geese?

parts.note: a sump is a pool or puddle

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the words that follow

parts.note: geese hiss, so to copy them is to hiss

indicators.note: hens running about scatter at random, so the letters scatter too

parts.note: these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Silly Scottish hens dash round a puddle imitating geese.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled hens go inside HISS. A sumph is a Scots blockhead, hence the Scots label in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumphishness is the state of being a sumph, a Scots word for a stupid, dull person.

clue.text: A prince folded ancient get-up? one could pack plenty more in it

definitions.text: one could pack plenty more in it

indicators.note: folding something back over itself turns it the other way round

parts.note: taken as written
a ras is an Ethiopian prince or chief
the toga was the dress of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A prince folds up his antique costume, and a big case would hold much more.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saratoga is a large travelling trunk, roomy enough to pack far more than a suitcase.

clue.text: Stopper and bolt drawn back

indicators.note: something drawn back is pulled the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to bolt food is to gulp it

explanation.surface: A bung and a door bolt are pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests a door fastening beside the stopper; it means swallow fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a stopper that fills a hole, as in a bath or sink.

clue.text: Ten freely breaking rule in vacation formerly

indicators.note: freely means without fixed order, so the letters are rearranged
something breaking into another splits it and sits inside

parts.note: a norm is a standard or rule
these three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten people freely break the rules while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-term was an old word for the time between law or university terms, when no term is sitting.

clue.text: Small carnivore making comeback in Bessarabia

indicators.note: making a comeback means the letters come back the other way
in says the letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: a run of letters inside the place name

explanation.surface: A small predator returns to its old haunts in Bessarabia, the region now split between Moldova and Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The rasse is a small civet cat of southern and south-east Asia.

clue.text: Cool phrase repeated after middle of intro

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes second
middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

parts.note: the third of five letters sits in the middle
a riff is a short musical phrase played over and over

explanation.surface: A musician describes a cool phrase looped after the middle of an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Triff is slang short for terrific, meaning cool or great.

clue.text: Last throw getting spattered in old fan …

indicators.note: spattered material splashes everywhere, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready for rearranging

explanation.surface: An old supporter gets spattered by a final throw, perhaps of something messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the archaic form; stalworth is the older spelling of stalwart.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, staunch supporter, and stalworth is the obsolete form of that word.

clue.text: … With such a noise? Watch out, fourth of punkahs following

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the word is rearranged
following places this letter after the rearranged word

parts.note: these five letters are rearranged

indicators.note: fourth of tells you to take the letter in fourth position

parts.note: P, U, N, then this letter in fourth place

explanation.surface: Continuing from the fan: watch out when the punkahs, big ceiling fans of colonial India, swing round noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 16, where the fan was a supporter; punkahs keep the fan theme going.
explanation.definitionFit: A thwack is a heavy smacking blow, and the word imitates the sound it makes.

clue.text: Lively dance, one followed by disapproving noises in ladies' organization

indicators.note: in sets these letters inside the organization's letters

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organization

indicators.note: followed by places the next piece straight after the first

parts.note: a means one
tuts are clicks of the tongue showing disapproval

explanation.surface: One energetic dancer at a Women's Institute event draws tuts from the other members.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a long-established British society for women, often pictured as genteel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Watusi was an energetic 1960s dance craze, also spelt Watutsi.

clue.text: Anaesthetic getting right inside a blood vessel

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: inside puts this abbreviation within the other word

parts.note: a vein is a blood vessel
RT is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A painkiller injected straight into a vein.
explanation.definitionFit: Avertin is a trade name for tribromoethanol, once given as a general anaesthetic.

clue.text: Singles contest in wrestling place, clubhouse excited?

parts.note: wrestlers fight on a mat
club split from house: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards, H for house
being up means being stirred up or excited

explanation.surface: A singles bout at a wrestling venue gets the club members excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubhouse' looks like one word for a building; it splits into club and house.
explanation.definitionFit: A match-up is a pairing of two opponents, like a one-on-one singles game.

clue.text: Albanian water buffalo in the open

parts.note: the arna is the wild water buffalo of India
out means out of doors or revealed

explanation.surface: An Albanian water buffalo grazing out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnaout is an old Turkish-derived term for an Albanian, especially an Albanian soldier.

clue.text: Concluded restraint tucking into pud freely

indicators.note: freely means the letters are free to fall in any order
tucking into something means going inside it

parts.note: these three letters are rearranged
a tie is something that restrains

explanation.surface: Restraint is over: someone tucks into pudding with abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pud is British slang for pudding, dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptie is an old verb for tying up or concluding, so uptied means wound up or finished.

clue.text: Cheers with HM coming on board? they're stunning

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: coming on to a vessel means going inside it, so these letters sit within

parts.note: on board means on a ship, and SS is a steamship
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A crew cheers as Her Majesty boards the ship, a stunning occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunning' looks like praise for the royal visit; it is literal. Being on board means being inside the ship's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasers are electric stun guns, so they are literally stunning weapons.

clue.text: Specialist giving word of honour taking bards back in

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, signalled with 'in'

parts.note: an oath is a solemn promise on one's honour

indicators.note: back means the poets are read from end to start

parts.note: bards are poets

explanation.surface: A consultant swears on their honour to take poets back in for treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath is a practitioner who specialises in manipulating bones and joints.

clue.text: Some of the family in Australia, including large part of it

indicators.note: including means holding the next part inside

parts.note: AUS is the abbreviation for Australia
NT is the Northern Territory, a large part of Australia

explanation.surface: Relatives living in Australia, spread over much of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives, members of one's wider family.

clue.text: Aristo, rarely French, he replaces one in large house

indicators.note: replaces means one piece is swapped out for another in the word

parts.note: a manor is a large country house
an means one, the letters swapped out
il is French for he

explanation.surface: A rarely seen French aristocrat takes over a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' appears to describe the aristocrat; it belongs to the wordplay, making he into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Milor is a rare form of milord, a continental term for an English nobleman.

clue.text: Pop king kept in chest

indicators.note: kept in means held inside the other word

parts.note: the bust is the chest
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A pop star crowned king keeps his treasures in a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop king' reads as a music star; Pop is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to pop, as a balloon does.

clue.text: Vigorous activity, quite often American, making money in Addis

definitions.meaning: first meaning: force or energy, often heard in US usage
second meaning: the currency of Ethiopia, whose capital is Addis Ababa

explanation.walkthrough: Addis is short for Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means vigour or whirring energy, and is also the name of Ethiopia's monetary unit.

clue.text: Mate, last changing location of island

indicators.note: the final letter moves to a new place, rearranging the end of the word

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A friend moves house, the latest change of address being an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, shortened to china. The A moves one place back.
explanation.definitionFit: Chian means belonging to Chios, the Greek island in the Aegean.

clue.text: Bairn set fire to money, left inside

parts.note: to light something is to set fire to it

indicators.note: inside places this abbreviation within the cash word

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A child sets fire to cash and leaves it there.
explanation.walkthrough: Bairn is the Scots word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Littlin is a Scots and northern word for a little one, a young child.

clue.text: Ice field, hostile round small latitude

indicators.note: round means going around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a foe is a hostile party, an enemy
L is the abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: A hostile expanse of ice at a small latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a sheet of floating ice, a field of ice on the sea.

clue.text: Centrepiece of cut in untidy tousles needing a shave?

indicators.note: untidy things are in disorder, so these letters are rearranged
in sets that letter inside the rearranged ones

parts.note: these seven letters are rearranged

indicators.note: the centrepiece of a three-letter word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle of three letters

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as playful: bristly stubble is what a shave removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Setulous means covered in small bristles, like a stubbly chin.

clue.text: Went (originally from Scandinavia), being tested skirting Norway

indicators.note: skirting means running around the edge of something, enclosing it

parts.note: tried means tested
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Someone, of Scandinavian origin, went off to be tested on the border of Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed note is etymology: trine comes from a Scandinavian word for to step.
explanation.definitionFit: Trine is an old verb meaning to go or march, so trined is its past tense.

clue.text: Leader of team in London club kicks

indicators.note: in sets that letter inside the club's name

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of team

explanation.surface: A team captain at a London football club kicks the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' wants to be a footballer's verb; here it is a plural noun, the bursts of speed a runner finds late in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick in racing is a sudden burst of pace, and spurts are such short bursts of speed.
